items.title: Dozens of Overnight Vehicle Break-Ins Across Mississauga End With One Arrest and a Continued Search
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, a string of vehicle break-ins that hit neighbourhoods across Mississauga between September 3 and September 6 has led to one arrest, with officers still searching for a second suspect. Police say the overnight break-ins involved 71 vehicles that were entered unlawfully, though no vehicles were taken and none were occupied at the time. Investigators allege valuables were stolen from inside the vehicles during the spree. A 34-year-old man with no fixed address has been charged with 46 counts of attempting to commit an indictable offence, 16 counts of theft under $5,000, 15 counts of mischief over $5,000 and one count of theft over $5,000, police say. He was also taken into custody on two outstanding warrants tied to separate fraud investigations, according to police. Peel police say they are still looking for a 34-year-old woman believed to have been involved alongside him in the break-ins.

items.title: Policorner Sets October 5 Date for a Mississauga Mayoral Debate Watched Well Beyond City Hall
items.summary: According to Policorner, a publication focused on Ontario provincial politics, the outlet will host a debate among Mississauga's leading mayoral candidates on Monday, October 5, at the Mississauga Civic Centre. Policorner says it decided to hold the 90-minute debate because the race has drawn unusually heavy provincial attention, given that it features two of only three people to have held the mayor's job since 1978. Premier Doug Ford weighed in on the race months before it began, telling reporters at a Mississauga construction site in March that he would send support to back Mayor Carolyn Parrish, according to Policorner. The outlet notes the contest pits Parrish, who has backing from Ford and his caucus, against her predecessor, a three-term mayor who left to lead the provincial Liberals and has spent much of the past three years opposing the Ford government. Two other candidates who finished second and third in the previous election are also competing for many of the same organizers and networks, Policorner reports.

items.title: Families of Victims Set to Address Court as Mississauga Man Faces Sentencing in Assisted-Suicide Case
items.summary: According to INsauga, friends and relatives of people who died after using items purchased online from Kenneth Law are expected to address the court this week as the Mississauga man faces a sentencing hearing. Law pleaded guilty in late May to 14 counts of aiding suicide in the deaths of 14 people across Ontario, including some victims who were minors. That plea came weeks before Law was set to stand trial on those charges along with 14 counts of first-degree murder connected to the same victims, and prosecutors have said they intend to withdraw the murder charges once he is sentenced. A conviction for aiding suicide can carry up to 14 years in prison, and lawyers for the Crown and defence are expected to argue for what each side considers an appropriate sentence. The hearing is also meant to give loved ones of those who died a chance to describe in court how Law's actions affected them. According to an agreed statement of facts read in court, Law ran several websites that sold sodium nitrite and other products that can be used for self-harm, and shipped roughly 1,200 packages to recipients in more than 40 countries, including close to 160 packages sent within Canada.

items.title: Coroner's Jury Rules 2023 Death of Mississauga Senior an Accident, Calls for Crisis-Team Reforms
items.summary: A coroner's inquest jury has ruled the 2023 death of 88-year-old Mississauga resident John Brownlie an accident and issued 18 recommendations aimed at reforming how police and mental health crisis teams respond to similar calls. According to the inquest, Brownlie, a retired schoolteacher, died from complications of a blunt impact neck injury after falling down a flight of stairs during a struggle with a Peel Regional Police officer inside his Mississauga home. The inquest heard that Brownlie had been identified as a candidate for a visit from the Crisis Outreach and Support Team, known as COAST, on September 13, 2023, a day after his wife, Doris, called a crisis line seeking help. Among the jury's recommendations are mandatory body cameras for officers responding to mental health crisis calls and revised protocols for how those officers make first contact. The recommendations are intended to prevent similar deaths during future encounters between police and people in mental health crisis, according to the inquest jury's findings.

items.title: Two Suspects Held for Bail as Peel Police Detail Arrests From a Nine-Month Gun Trafficking Probe
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, Peel Regional Police have released an update on Project Red Zone, a nine-month undercover investigation that has resulted in four arrests and the seizure of 23 firearms along with 950 rounds of ammunition tied to a firearms trafficking network. Of the four people arrested and charged in the case, two have since been released while two remain in custody pending a bail hearing, the Star reports. Police say one of the recovered firearms has been linked to a fatal shooting in Mississauga, while 14 of the guns have been connected to other shootings across the Greater Toronto Area. The Star reports the update was shared publicly on Tuesday as police continue working through the case. Investigators had previously said 15 of the 23 seized firearms originated in the United States before making their way into the trafficking network.

items.title: Early 2027 Launch Planned as Mississauga Opens Its Whistleblower Hotline to the Public
items.summary: According to a staff report set to go before Mississauga's general committee on Wednesday, the city plans to launch an expanded whistleblower hotline for residents sometime in the first three months of 2027. The city established its original Whistleblower Program in 2014, giving employees a confidential channel to anonymously flag workplace wrongdoing, but the new fraud and waste hotline will extend that same option to the general public. Amy Truong, the city's internal audit director, wrote in the report that the program has spent the past decade supporting accountability, ethical conduct and a workplace culture where concerns can be raised without fear of reprisal. The report describes the expanded hotline as an independent and confidential reporting mechanism meant to strengthen accountability and reinforce public trust in the integrity of city operations. Once it is running, both city workers and members of the public will be able to use it to report concerns tied to fraud, waste or wrongdoing that could affect the city's operations. Truong's report also frames the changes as an effort to strengthen transparency and public confidence in how the city governs and oversees itself. The move follows discussions among councillors and staff back in March about whether Mississauga should also hire an auditor general to bolster public accountability.

items.title: A Report of an Armed Man in Cooksville Led Police to Four Arrests and $65,000 in Drugs
items.summary: According to CTV News, Peel Regional Police say four people have been arrested after a September 7 call reporting a man armed with a gun inside a vehicle near Hurontario Street and Dundas Street West, in the city's Cooksville area. Officers who responded found the man in possession of an illegal firearm along with a separate loaded magazine, according to police. A search of the scene turned up a quantity of suspected cocaine and fentanyl that police estimated to be worth about $65,000. Investigators later executed a search warrant at a Mississauga residence, where three more people were arrested. Police say Olamilekan Jimoh, 26, of Mississauga, faces the most charges, including careless storage of a firearm, failing to comply with an undertaking, and four counts of possession for the purpose of trafficking. Modupe Abijo, 52, and Omobodunrin Jimoh, 28, both of Mississauga, were each charged with four counts of possession for the purpose of trafficking, while Cleo Romi Reynods, 45, of Toronto, was charged with failing to comply with a release order.
